question.worked_solution:
Recall that 

- ${max}_{x\in S}f(x)$ is the largest output value, while

- $\operatorname{arg}⁡{max}_{x\in S}f(x)$ is an input in $S$ where that largest output occurs.

On the other hand,

- ${min}_{x\in S}f(x)$ is the smallest output value, while

- $\operatorname{arg}⁡{min}_{x\in S}f(x)$ is an input in $S$ where that smallest output occurs.

Here, the outputs are $-8,$ $1,$ $3,$ and $10.$ 

- The largest output is $10,$ and it occurs at $x=2.$

- The smallest output is $-8,$ and it occurs at $x=4.$

Therefore, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{max}_{x\in S}f(x) & =10 \\ \operatorname{arg}⁡{max}_{x\in S}f(x) & =2 \\ {min}_{x\in S}f(x) & =-8 \\ \operatorname{arg}⁡{min}_{x\in S}f(x) & =4\end{aligned}
$$
